best/liska.name: Fox
profile: Foxes live in forests, along meadow edges and near human settlements. They seek shelter in burrows, among roots or in dense vegetation. They hunt small animals for food, but also eat fruit and readily available scraps. A narrow trail, a print in the mud or a russet tail disappearing into the undergrowth may reveal their presence.

A fox is curious, quick to learn and cautious. It often travels alone, although it may share its territory with a mate and cubs. Rather than face a direct confrontation, it prefers speed, cover and an evasive move; it usually bites in self-defence when it cannot escape. Its Dodge ability helps it resist one declared attack during a combat.

In an adventure, a fox might carry supplies away from camp or lead the party to a den in forgotten ruins. The heroes may discover that the apparently cheeky thief is simply gathering food for its cubs. Patient observation is often more useful than a chase.
best/liska.abilityEffect: Once per combat, after an attack target is declared, gains +2 Defense against that attack.

best/vlk.name: Wolf
profile: Wolves live in forests, on open plains and in mountain areas where they can find prey and enough space. A pack is usually a family group that works together to hunt and care for its young. Tracks left by several animals and distant howling may suggest that the party has entered their territory.

Wolves are alert, quick to learn and capable of cooperation. They usually avoid people; they may defend themselves when protecting their young, cornered or left with no other choice. A lone wolf does not necessarily mean an immediate attack, but it is worth watching the surroundings. In the game, Pack Attack applies if another wolf has attacked the same target during that round.

The party might discover an injured animal, a den they have approached too closely or a trail shared by wolves and people. A good solution may involve going around their territory and removing the cause of the conflict. A wolf is not automatically an evil opponent: its behaviour should fit the situation.

strings.Pokud stejný cíl v tomto kole napadl ale: If at least one other wolf attacked the same target this round, this wolf gains +1 to its final Attack result.

best/krysa.name: Rat
profile: Rats stay wherever they can find food, warmth and shelter: in cellars, granaries, stables and underground passages. Tiny tracks, gnawed sacks and rustling behind a wall reveal their presence. They often share hiding places and remember safe routes to supplies.

They are cautious and quick, usually trying to hide from a larger opponent. They may bite when cornered or protecting a nest; a large cluster of rats can block a narrow passage for the party. Agility is their strength, while their small size limits their physical strength. In the game, Slip Away helps them avoid a subsequent physical hit.

An encounter need not end in combat. The party can secure its supplies, find a hole in the wall or lure the rats away from the route. If unusually large numbers gather in one place, they may point to hidden food or a forgotten passage.

strings.1× za souboj po obdržení zranění získá +: Once per combat, after taking damage, gains +2 Defense against the next physical attack.

best/netopyr.name: Bat
profile: Bats rest in caves, hollow trees and abandoned towers. At dusk they set out in search of food; ordinary small bats mainly hunt insects. They navigate in darkness using echoes of their own calls and may share their shelters in large colonies.

They are not natural enemies of the heroes. A disturbed colony can, however, turn a quiet passage into a chaotic stream of wings and sounds. A bat is agile in the air but physically weak. Its Flight ability increases physical defense against melee attacks only while it can actually fly.

The Game Master can use bats as a sign of a nearby cave or an open route outside. The heroes can let the animals fly past undisturbed and continue instead of drawing their weapons. Unusual behavior in a colony may provide a clue that something is disturbing its shelter.

strings.Dokud může létat, získává +1 FO proti út: While it can fly, gains +1 PDEF against melee attacks.

best/divoka-kocka.name: Wildcat
profile: The wildcat lives in quiet forests, thickets and rocky places where it can find small prey and safe hiding places. It is usually solitary and moves silently; a paw print, scratches on a trunk or a brief flash of eyes among the branches may reveal its presence.

It is alert and patient, preferring escape to an unnecessary confrontation. When defending its young or unable to retreat, however, it can spring forward fiercely and use both claws and teeth. It relies on mobility and surprise. Its Pounce ability is most useful at the start of combat.

By following a wildcat, the party might discover a quiet shelter, a small trail or a place recently disturbed by another creature. Earning its trust requires patience and distance; it is not a tame house cat, and approaching too quickly may frighten it.

strings.V prvním kole souboje má +1 k výslednému: Gains +1 to the final Attack result during the first round of combat.

best/toulavy-pes.name: Stray Dog
profile: A stray dog is often a lost or abandoned human companion. It wanders around villages, markets and roads in search of food, water and a dry place to rest. Some dogs live alone, while others join a small group to seek safety together.

It can recognize moods, familiar smells and simple human behavior. Hunger or bad experiences may make it distrustful, but not every stray dog is aggressive. Its barking may warn of danger, guard a shelter it has found or draw attention to something the party has not yet noticed. It has no special combat ability.

An encounter may begin a search for its owner or an effort to help an entire village. The dog might guard a lost backpack, return to an empty house or follow the trail of someone it knows. The heroes should respect its distance and earn its trust gradually, without trying to grab it by force.

best/divoke-prase.name: Wild Boar
profile: A wild boar searches for food in forests, thickets and along the edges of fields. Churned earth, tracks in wet mud and bark rubbed off trees reveal its movements. Females with young stay in groups, while an adult male may roam alone.

It has an excellent sense of smell, a powerful body and can quickly gather speed. It usually prefers to retreat, but may attack fiercely if surprised at close range or defending its young. Surrounding it is unwise. Its Charge ability strengthens its first attack only if it actually has room for a running start.

In an adventure, a herd might block a forest path or forage somewhere hunger has driven it to. The heroes can retreat, find another route or discover why the animals have left their usual territory. Freshly churned ground may also uncover a lost object or an old entrance underground.

strings.V prvním kole, pokud může zaútočit po ro: During the first round, if it can attack after a running start, gains +2 to its final Attack result.

best/jedovaty-had.name: Venomous Snake
profile: A venomous snake hides under stones, among roots, in tall grass or in warm cracks in the rock. This bestiary entry represents a game creature with a venomous bite, rather than every snake in the real world. It usually lives alone, seeking prey and a safe shelter.

It is inconspicuous and can wait motionless for a long time. It generally does not attack a larger creature as prey; danger mainly arises when it is startled or cornered. The party should watch where it steps and reaches. Its game venom only takes effect after a bite that causes damage, and the subsequent effect is specified precisely in its ability.

A snake may guard a location simply because it has chosen to shelter there. Taking another route or leaving it room is often wiser than fighting. In a story, shed skin and small tracks might lead to a warm spring or a room that has remained unopened for years.

strings.Pokud uštknutí způsobí alespoň 1 zranění: If a bite deals at least 1 damage, the target loses 1 additional HP at the end of each of the next 2 rounds; this effect does not stack.

best/medved.name: Bear
profile: Bears inhabit Elaria's vast forests, mountain valleys and remote slopes. They shelter in thickets, rocky hollows or beneath fallen trees. Large tracks, dug-up ground, damaged beehives and scratches on trunks reveal their presence. They seek food according to the season; fruit, honey, small prey and easily accessible supplies attract them.

They spend most of their time alone. The main exception is a mother with cubs, who protects their safety far more fiercely than her own comfort. A bear remembers places where food is available and quickly recognizes where danger is coming from. No leader or evil intention controls it. Being surprised at close range, injured or cornered can, however, turn a peaceful animal into an extremely dangerous opponent.

In combat, it relies on strength and endurance. Mighty Blow strengthens a melee attack once per combat, making it truly risky to remain within reach of its paws. Leaving room to retreat and keeping away from cubs can prevent conflict. A displaced bear near a village may be a clue to a disturbed forest, a ruined den or someone deliberately luring it toward human homes.

strings.1× za souboj získá +2 k výslednému ÚTOKU: Once per combat, gains +2 to the final result of a melee Attack.

best/krokodyl.name: Crocodile
profile: A crocodile lives in warm rivers, swamps and flooded ruins. It can remain almost invisible in muddy water for a long time; only its eyes and ripples around its nostrils show above the surface. It seeks places where other creatures drink, wade or approach the bank. Sliding tracks in mud and a conspicuously deserted watering hole may reveal its territory.

It is a patient hunter that conserves its strength and chooses the right moment to attack. It usually acts alone, although several individuals may gather around a rich food source. Such a gathering is not an obedient pack. A crocodile responds to prey, space and immediate threats; it may defend a sheltered retreat or nesting place even when it is not hungry.

Its greatest advantage is surprise near water. Crush makes the injured target's next attack harder, while Tough Hide reduces the first physical damage it takes each round. Going around the bank, using a sturdy footbridge or choosing another crossing is often safer. A crocodile may guard access to ruins simply by settling there; killing it need not be necessary to resolve the situation.

strings.Pokud způsobí alespoň 3 zranění jedním ú: If one attack deals at least 3 damage, the target gets −1 to its final Attack result next round. Tough Hide reduces the first physical damage the crocodile takes each round by 2 (minimum 0).

best/orel.name: Eagle
profile: An eagle nests on rocky ledges, tall trees and abandoned towers that give it a view over a wide area. Above mountains and open countryside, it uses air currents to circle for long periods. Its nest is usually difficult to reach and may occupy a spot the party needs as a lookout or a route across a cliff face.

It has excellent eyesight and reacts quickly to movement. It hunts smaller prey and usually keeps away from noisy groups. It often lives as part of a pair defending a nest and young, rather than an organized combat group. Attacking a large human is more likely a defense of its nesting ground or a response to a direct threat than an ordinary way of finding food.

Dive Attack strengthens its strike once per combat, but temporarily lowers its physical defense afterward. In flight, it uses height, speed and open space; circling before an attack gives observant characters a chance to find cover. An eagle can lead the party to a mountain pass, reveal the movement of prey or signal a disturbance in the landscape. Rescuing an injured bird or safely going around a nest can also provide a peaceful encounter.

strings.1× za souboj získá +2 k výslednému ÚTOKU: Once per combat, gains +2 to the final Attack result; after this attack, has −1 PDEF until the start of its next turn.

best/jelen.name: Deer
profile: Deer inhabit forests, meadows and open mountain valleys. They forage in clearings and along quiet forest edges from which they can quickly withdraw into cover. Hoof prints, nibbled shoots and rubbed bark mark their presence. In Elaria's stories, an impressive stag may symbolize a particular forest, but an actual encounter still follows the behavior of a wild animal.

Deer gather according to their surroundings and the season; males may travel separately and defend their space more vigorously when competing. Caution helps them survive more than a willingness to fight. An unfamiliar smell or noise usually makes them stop, listen and retreat. Antlers are dangerous when the animal feels trapped or someone blocks its way.

Flee increases physical defense when the deer chooses to escape instead of attacking. Leaving an open route therefore suits its natural response to danger. The party can follow its tracks to water, find an abandoned fawn or discover why wildlife has disappeared from the forest. Unusual herd behavior may warn of a predator, fire or disturbed territory without the deer itself being an enemy.

strings.Pokud se místo útoku rozhodne utéct, zís: If it chooses to flee instead of attacking, gains +2 PDEF until its next turn.

best/vesnican.name: Villager
profile: A villager represents an ordinary inhabitant of Elaria: a farmer, shepherd, woodcutter or someone whose daily work keeps a settlement alive. They know local roads, neighbors, the weather and changes in the surrounding landscape. News of unusual tracks, an empty field or a cart that never arrived may be more valuable to adventurers than a scholarly map. Their knowledge comes from experience rather than adventuring training.

They usually live with a family and rely on help from neighbors. Their decisions are influenced by the mayor, village council, local lord and the community's unwritten rules. Their goals are often the safety of loved ones, a good harvest and survival through another winter. They may welcome or distrust strangers depending on the village's experiences. Fear, debt or pressure from someone more powerful may explain behavior that initially seems hostile.

A villager has no special combat ability, and an open confrontation is seriously dangerous for them. When they defend themselves, they are often protecting a home, supplies or family. Conversation, proof of good intentions and practical help can change a relationship faster than threats. In a story, they may be a witness, guide or someone hiding information for fear of the consequences. The stat profile describes an ordinary resident; the individual character determines their personality and past.

best/obchodnik.name: Merchant
profile: A merchant connects villages, cities and distant markets. They may own a shop, lead a caravan or travel with a single cart and a few crates of goods. They know prices, demand and dangerous stretches of road. They notice where salt is scarce, who is buying up iron and why medicinal herbs have suddenly disappeared. Such changes can reveal a developing conflict before public proclamations do.

Their main goal is usually to maintain their business and reputation, but an individual merchant may put family, guild or a major customer first. They often work with carriers, guards and suppliers; a wealthy trader has an extensive network of contacts. An ability to deal with people does not automatically imply dishonesty. Some bargain hard but fairly, while others conceal faulty goods or trade in things they prefer not to ask about.

Haggle gives them an advantage in a social encounter based on Charisma. In combat, they usually protect their life and goods, seeking an agreement or help from guards. The party can offer protection, information or a service instead of money. A lost shipment, counterfeit coins and an unusually cheap artifact are natural starting points for adventures. Assuming every trader is a fraud could mean overlooking a potential long-term ally.

strings.Při sociálním střetu založeném na Charis: Gains +1 to the result of a roll in a social encounter based on Charisma.

best/kovar.name: Blacksmith
profile: A blacksmith works in a settlement, a city workshop or near a military camp. Depending on their specialty, they make and repair tools, horseshoes, weapons and pieces of equipment. They need a reliable supply of metal, fuel and commissions, so they are keenly aware of trouble on roads and in mines. Hammer blows, the smell of hot metal and customers bringing items essential to their livelihood identify the smithy.

They are used to demanding work and practical problem-solving. They may work alone, with family or supervise apprentices and journeymen; in a city, they may follow guild rules. Their strength says nothing about their personality. They could be a patient master, a proud specialist or someone irritated by broken promises. They often value good materials and honest work more than impressive speeches.

They have no special combat ability, and workshop experience is not the same as warrior training. When threatened, however, they may firmly defend their workshop and loved ones. They can help the party recognize unusual metalwork, trace the origin of equipment or repair a damaged item as the story allows. A stolen commission, a missing apprentice or metal that behaves strangely when worked can open an adventure in which the blacksmith remains a partner rather than an obstacle.

best/lovec.name: Hunter
profile: A hunter spends much of their life beyond the safety of settlements. They travel forest trails, track game and know where to find water or shelter. Their home may be a solitary cabin or a village to which they return with their catch. They distinguish ordinary tracks from those of an injured animal, an unusual predator or someone trying to conceal their movements.

They usually work alone or in a small group where silence and mutual trust matter. They act independently, but may serve a forest warden, supply a village or protect an estate. Their goals are often a livelihood, the safety of familiar territory and returning from another expedition. An honest hunter and a poacher may have similar skills, but their relationships with local people and rules will be very different.

Precise Shot strengthens a ranged attack once per combat. They seek an advantage in a prepared position, a clear view and distance; reckless melee combat may not suit their experience. They can guide the party through dangerous terrain, teach them to read tracks or ask for help with something ordinary wildlife cannot explain. Respect for their knowledge and a willingness to heed warnings the rest of the village ignores often determine how negotiations go.

strings.1× za souboj získá +2 k výslednému ÚTOKU: Once per combat, gains +2 to the final result of a ranged Attack.

best/zlodej.name: Thief
profile: A thief may grow up in city alleys, operate in a marketplace or burgle houses in a wealthy neighborhood. This profile describes someone accustomed to acquiring things discreetly and finding gaps in other people's attention. They study guards' habits, crowds and escape opportunities. An abandoned warehouse or a room above an inn may serve as a hideout, but an experienced thief dislikes revealing their true base.

They work alone, with a trusted partner or for a group that divides tasks among lookouts, thieves and fences. If they belong to a guild, they may answer to its rules and leaders. Money, debt, survival, revenge or a desire for a particular object can motivate them. Their ability to steal does not determine whom they are willing to harm. Some avoid violence, while others remove obstacles without hesitation.

Sneak Attack gives them an advantage once per combat against a target that has not yet acted that round. A thief therefore benefits from surprise and acting quickly, while a long, open confrontation may jeopardize their escape route. The party can catch, hire or persuade them to return a stolen item. An interesting encounter can also arise when they know about a greater crime and offer information in exchange for protection from their own employer.

strings.1× za souboj získá +2 k výslednému ÚTOKU: Once per combat, gains +2 to the final Attack result if the target has not yet acted this round.

best/bandita.name: Bandit
profile: A bandit makes a living by ambushing travelers, extortion and stealing supplies. They seek a hideout beside abandoned roads, in a forest, quarry or ruined stronghold from which they can watch passing carts. They may have entered this life as a deserter, someone in debt or a willing robber. A shared profile therefore does not imply a shared origin or equal willingness to take risks.

They most often operate in a small gang. Some keep watch, others select targets, and others maintain contact with a fence. They obey a leader while that leader offers profit, safety or inspires enough fear. Bandits usually want to acquire property with as few losses of their own as possible. An unprotected cart is therefore more attractive than a prepared party, and a clearly superior opponent may quickly turn determination into flight.

A bandit has no special combat ability. A gang's danger comes from numbers, ambush and knowledge of the location. They may demand a ransom, block a road or intimidate people without intending to fight to the death. Discovering lookouts, securing another route or making an offer that undermines the group's cohesion can resolve the confrontation. A captured bandit may know the hideout and who ordered the robberies, but will consider who can protect them from retaliation.

best/vudce-banditu.name: Bandit Leader
profile: A bandit leader has turned several individual robbers into a group with hideouts, lookouts and a plan. They are often an experienced fighter, a former commander or someone who rose through courage and an ability to secure loot. Their base is better protected than an ordinary camp and may hold supplies, prisoners and records of whom the gang sells stolen goods to.

They keep members together through a share of profits, personal loyalty or fear. A capable leader assigns tasks and knows their followers' weaknesses; a cruel leader may overlook resentment until it is too late. Their goal might be wealth, control of a trade route or service to a hidden patron. They do not necessarily treat subordinates like strangers, and relationships within the gang may decide the entire conflict.

Commander strengthens one allied bandit's attack each round while the leader remains conscious. Their presence therefore affects the whole group's combat. The party can seek evidence against the patron, disrupt supplies or negotiate the release of prisoners. A loss of authority, a dispute over sharing loot or an exposed lie can be as effective a story development as a direct fight. The leader judges a proposed truce, however, by what they believe they stand to lose.

strings.Dokud je při vědomí, 1 spojenec bandita: While the leader is conscious, one allied bandit gains +1 to its final Attack result each round.
strings.Jak použít Vůdce banditů: How to use the Bandit Leader

best/zoldner.name: Mercenary
profile: A mercenary offers combat experience for payment. They may guard a caravan, protect a mine, serve a city council or fight in a foreign army. Their backgrounds vary: some left the army, while others have spent their lives moving between short contracts. Their equipment reflects their means and the work they accept. Before a journey, an experienced mercenary checks supplies, the condition of weapons and the abilities of future allies.

They work independently or in a company led by a captain. Loyalty may rest on a contract, personal honor or a long campaign together. Payment alone does not mean they will do anything; some refuse attacks on civilians or jobs that conflict with their convictions. Others care only about the reward. Most, however, need to survive and maintain a reputation to secure future work.

They have no special ability, but their combat values represent someone accustomed to real fighting. They usually aim to complete the task and observe the contract's terms. If they oppose the party, it can help to discover whom they protect, what they were told and where their obligation ends. Withheld pay, a dishonest employer or an order that violates the contract may create room for negotiation. A mercenary can become both an opponent and a dependable ally within one story.

best/vojak.name: Soldier
profile: A soldier serves in an organized army, a city guard or a border fortress garrison. They have learned to handle equipment, guard an assigned location and carry out tasks alongside others. An ordinary day includes training, shifts, marches and equipment maintenance. They may know their city better than a visitor while knowing very little about why their commander accepted a particular order.

They belong to a unit with a clear chain of command. Their commander, oath and relationships with fellow soldiers influence their decisions without removing their own conscience. They may have chosen service for pay, family tradition or to protect their home. They are not automatically aggressive: at a checkpoint, their aim may be to control passage and maintain order. A tired recruit and a veteran will judge the same situation differently.

They have no special ability; their strength lies in training and cooperation. In a conflict, they may call for help, hold their assigned position or detain a suspect. The party can present evidence, establish what an order actually says and approach the responsible commander. A soldier may witness abuse of power, act on incorrect information or be an ally needing help beyond their garrison's reach. A uniform defines their service, not their entire personality.

best/lucistnik.name: Archer
profile: An archer is a trained fighter specializing in ranged attacks. They can be found on city walls, defending a mountain pass, with a military unit or among caravan guards. They pay attention to their field of view, obstacles and their supply of arrows. A favorable position allows them to carry out their task more safely than a spot where an opponent can approach unnoticed.

They may serve a commander or act independently as a hired bowman. Within a group, they need to coordinate with those protecting access to their position. Their aim is often to stop an advance, support allies or cover a retreat. Archery training alone says nothing about cruelty or honor; the difference between a village defender and a robber on a cliff comes from the assignment and the individual's choices.

Covering Fire strengthens a ranged attack in a round during which the archer has not faced a melee attack. Maintaining distance is therefore central to their fighting style. Cover, blocked sightlines and thoughtful movement change the conditions of an encounter. The party may meet an archer on an escort mission, on patrol or when they are aiming at the wrong person on someone else's orders. Negotiations must account for their position and the possibility of other defenders waiting nearby.

strings.Pokud v tomto kole nezažil útok zblízka,: If the archer has not been attacked at close range this round, gains +1 to the final result of a ranged Attack.

best/rytir.name: Knight
profile: A knight combines combat training with rank, an oath or service to a particular order. They may administer a small estate, travel on a mission or lead the defense of a fortress. Their equipment, emblem and entourage often reveal whom they serve. Good armor requires care and resources; a knighthood therefore brings relationships and obligations an ordinary warrior may not have.

Not every knight fulfills the ideal of a just protector. Some defend the vulnerable, while others chiefly protect their family or privileges. They usually have a lord, order or personal oath against which they measure their decisions. They may travel with a squire, companions or soldiers, but a lone knight on a quest is just as possible. Honor and reputation can motivate them more strongly than money.

Parry increases defense against the first physical attack aimed at them each round. In a direct confrontation, they are therefore a reliable defender and an opponent to take seriously. A conflict between an order and an oath may create room for conversation. A knight may demand evidence, accept a shared mission or protect someone whose guilt they do not yet know about. The story gains depth when the party discovers what they consider their duty and what they fear losing.

strings.1× za kolo získá +2 k OBRANĚ proti první: Once per round, gains +2 Defense against the first physical attack aimed at the knight.

best/kouzelnik.name: Wizard
profile: A wizard develops magic through study, practice or guidance from an experienced teacher. In Elaria, they may work in an academy, a private study, at court or travel in search of rare knowledge. Their base often holds books, tools and materials needed for research. An individual wizard may belong to a tradition that closely guards its knowledge or passes it on to new students.

They usually consider connections and prepare ways of dealing with difficult situations. Great learning, however, does not rule out vanity, mistakes or poor judgment of people. They may serve a school, a patron or their own research. They seek new knowledge, access to artifacts and time to work; there is no reason to assume every mage wants power over others. Their personality and the limits of their experiments determine their relationship with the party.

This profile uses Fire Bolt and Magic Shield. It has an effective magic attack and increased magic defense against the first such attack each round. Its abilities therefore call for a different approach than an ordinary armed opponent. A lost scroll, dangerous experiment or the need to transport an unusual object safely can lead to cooperation. Negotiations may involve exchanging knowledge and services; a wizard's secret need not be evil, but may have consequences they do not yet understand.

strings.Může používat magický útok s bonusem kou: Can make a magic attack with a +3 spell bonus. Gains +2 MDEF against the first magic attack each round.

best/lecitel.name: Healer
profile: A healer helps people after injuries, during illness and on demanding journeys. They may care for a village, work in a temple or army, or accompany adventurers. Their knowledge comes from study, tradition or practical service to an experienced teacher. They need supplies and a safe place to work, so shortages of remedies or violence nearby also affect those who need their help most.

They often have strong community ties and know the stories of the people who come to them. They may work alone, with assistants or under an order's rules. Caring for others, faith, obligation or an ordinary livelihood can motivate them. A willingness to help does not mean unlimited strength or an obligation to trust everyone. A healer may refuse a journey that would leave an entire settlement without care.

Healing lets them restore four Health to themselves or an ally instead of attacking once per combat. In battle, they therefore seek safety and access to whoever needs help; taking them out of action can change the whole group's prospects. The party can protect them, obtain missing supplies or help uncover the cause of recurring injuries. An interesting conflict arises when a healer treats both sides of a dispute and someone tries to exploit their neutrality.

strings.1× za souboj obnoví sobě nebo spojenci 4: Once per combat, restores 4 HP to themself or an ally instead of attacking.

best/slechtic.name: Noble
profile: A noble gained their position through inheritance, service or a ruler's decision. They may administer an estate, reside at court or represent their family in negotiations. Their residence and wealth depend on their holdings and actual resources. Even an impressive title may conceal a debt-ridden estate, hostile neighbors or a family that has already lost most of its influence.

They belong to a network of family relationships, obligations and social expectations. Subjects, stewards and allies may support their decisions, but also constrain them. They seek the safety of their estate, prestige or continuity of their family; an individual may instead prioritize justice, personal interests or revenge. They can be courteous or threatening according to their personality and circumstances. A seemingly small insult may matter if it undermines their authority in front of others.

Authority provides a bonus in a social encounter only where the noble has genuine social authority. A title is therefore not a universal means of controlling strangers. The party can offer a service, establish a right or expose a discrepancy between public reputation and reality. A boundary dispute, a missing heir or a problem concealed by a steward provide opportunities for adventure. A noble can be a quest giver, an obstacle or an ally whose power has clear limits.

strings.Při sociálním střetu, kde má skutečnou s: In a social encounter where the noble has genuine social authority, gains +2 to the Charisma result.

best/kral-kralovna.name: King / Queen
profile: A king or queen leads a country, but history, laws and the throne's actual support shape their rule. The monarch may reside in a palace, lead a campaign or administer the kingdom from a temporary court. This profile represents a ruler as a person in a significant role; an entire realm's strength cannot be expressed through their personal combat values alone.

They govern through advisers, officials, commanders and local administrators. Information reaches them through people with their own interests, so they may not know the true state of a distant province. Their goal may be peace, prosperity, preserving the dynasty or expanding their power. Good intentions do not guarantee good decisions, and a harsh decision does not necessarily arise from cruelty. Their relationship with their subjects and willingness to accept uncomfortable truths shape their character.

Royal Authority improves dealings with subjects, but its bonus does not apply in combat. The monarch usually relies on the court's protection and organization rather than personally dueling every opponent. The party can deliver evidence, receive a commission or expose who is distorting information before it reaches the throne. An audience is interesting when both sides have a specific need and face time pressure. Saving the monarch may not be enough if the source of the threat remains in their inner circle.

strings.Při jednání s poddanými získá +2 k výsle: When dealing with their subjects, gains +2 to the Charisma result; this bonus does not apply in combat.

best/goblin.name: Goblin
profile: Goblins are small humanoids of Elaria who seek a place on the fringes of more powerful societies. They live in caves, ravines, abandoned mines and ruins that offer shelter and useful materials. Various stories link their origins to ancient underground settlements; individual tribes preserve their own legends, however, and may not know a shared history. Small tracks, improvised repairs and piles of things others consider rubbish reveal their homes.

They are practical, observant and quick to spot an opportunity. Low status or rough manners are not evidence of stupidity. They usually live in families and groups led by a chief, sometimes under the influence of a stronger neighbor. They seek food, safety and useful objects. Some gangs raid, while others trade or collect leftovers from other expeditions. Hunger, fear, leadership and experiences with their surroundings influence their aggression.

In combat, they seek superior numbers, cover and an escape route. Duck for Cover increases defense against a ranged attack once per combat. An exposed goblin may retreat, warn its group or offer a deal. The party can discover what drove the gang from its original shelter, whom it must pay in supplies and who forces it to raid. Food, safe passage or removing a shared threat can provide a genuine reason to negotiate.

strings.1× za souboj získá +2 OBRANA proti jedno: Once per combat, gains +2 Defense against one ranged attack.

best/goblin-lucistnik.name: Goblin Archer
profile: A goblin archer comes from the same surroundings as other goblins, but has learned to rely on distance and favorable positions. They guard cave entrances, watch trails above ravines or cover their gang from the windows of abandoned buildings. Their bow and arrows may be homemade, traded for or collected after other expeditions. A supply of arrows and knowledge of nearby hiding places matter as much as the weapon itself.

They usually work with other group members. One watches the approach, another lures the target out, and the archer waits for the right moment. They obey a chief or a more experienced commander, but may primarily be protecting their own family and shelter. They can plan and learn from failure. If the gang has no reason to fight, they may simply warn strangers to stay away from its supplies instead of ambushing them.

Quick Reposition improves physical defense against the next melee attack until their next turn after they make a ranged attack. This suits a style of shooting and immediately changing position. Open ground without cover or a blocked view makes it harder to use the surroundings. The party can discover their position, offer a safe retreat or find out why they guard this particular passage. An alert archer often knows more about nearby events than a gang member who stays deep in camp.

strings.Po útoku na dálku získá +1 FO proti nejb: After a ranged attack, gains +1 PDEF against the next melee attack until its next turn.

best/kobold.name: Kobold
profile: Kobolds are small humanoids whose communities settle in Elaria's underground passages, rocky hollows and old mines. They often explain their origins through legends of ancient guardians of the depths and powerful, scaled patrons. Each settlement interprets these stories differently. Narrow passages, small tools and carefully used alcoves show that their homes are adapted to smaller inhabitants.

They rely on their group and a division of labor. Guards, gatherers, craftspeople and scouts have their own tasks, which may be directed by elders, a chief or a revered patron. Kobolds are cautious and practical; they learn where it is safe and which obstacles large opponents cannot easily overcome. They want to preserve their shelter, supplies and community's position. Conflict often arises over intrusions into their territory, unclear agreements or pressure from a stronger creature.

Teamwork increases their attack when another kobold is beside the target. A lone individual may therefore try to bring help rather than attempt a heroic duel. The party can seek a route underground, negotiate access or help the community escape an abusive patron. Preparing their surroundings is part of their way of life, but the specific adventure determines any traps and their effects. Offering safety and honoring agreements can turn distrust into a practical alliance.

strings.Pokud je vedle cíle alespoň 1 další kobo: If at least 1 other kobold is next to the target, gains +1 to the final Attack result.

best/hobgoblin.name: Hobgoblin
profile: Hobgoblins build stronger, more organized communities than many smaller gangs. In Elaria, they can be found in fortified camps, occupied strongholds and along the borders of disputed territories. Their traditions emphasize service, order and collective strength. Individual companies have different origins: some come from old military families, while others formed around a capable commander during wartime.

They are intelligent, disciplined and able to plan for the long term. Within a group, they have clear roles and expect orders to be followed; authority is tied to rank and results. They may serve their own chief, a local ruler or work as a contracted unit. They seek supplies, safe territory and recognition of their group's strength. Strictness does not automatically mean reckless aggression. A carefully prepared agreement may benefit a commander more than losses in battle.

Shield Wall increases physical defense when at least one other hobgoblin is in combat. Fighting together therefore strongly supports their style. Disrupted organization, an exposed mistaken order or a threatened supply route can change the situation before combat begins. The party can negotiate with the commander over passage, prisoners or a shared enemy. A hobgoblin who has given their word and has reason to keep it may be a more reliable partner than a polished human with unclear interests.

strings.Pokud je v boji alespoň jeden další hobg: If at least one other hobgoblin is in combat, gains +2 PDEF.

best/bugbear.name: Bugbear
profile: A bugbear is a powerful humanoid that seeks Elaria's rugged forests, rocky ravines and abandoned buildings. Its strength draws attention, but its ability to hide and wait can be just as dangerous. Local legends say some groups descend from ancient forest clans, while others have long lived beside goblin gangs. In ruins, it chooses a position from which it can watch the approach and act quickly.

It may live alone, with a family or as a strong ally of a larger gang. Sometimes it accepts a chief's leadership; at other times, others follow its own authority. It is not merely muscle without a mind: it can assess risks, remember routes and exploit other people's inattention. Food, shelter, payment or protecting loved ones may motivate it. Some bugbears ambush travelers, but appearance alone does not determine their character.

Ambush adds to its attack in the first round if it was not detected before combat. Careful scouting can therefore remove its main advantage before the confrontation. Once revealed, it remains a powerful opponent that is dangerous to underestimate. The party may encounter a hired guard, a solitary resident of ruins or someone refusing to leave a place connected to their family. Discovering the true reason for its presence opens up solutions beyond attacking.

strings.V prvním kole souboje získá +2 k výsledn: During the first round of combat, gains +2 to the final Attack result if it was not detected before the fight.

best/gnom.name: Gnome
profile: Gnomes establish small settlements, workshops and hidden homes in Elaria's hills or beneath old cities. Their traditions combine craftsmanship, curiosity and the study of unusual phenomena. Family stories often recall ancestors who safely crossed the boundary between practical invention and magical knowledge. A gnome's home usually makes good use of space, holds many tools and contains objects whose purpose a visitor will not immediately recognize.

They are intelligent and enjoy finding solutions beyond those offered by custom. They live in families or communities where experienced masters, researchers and elders may gain respected positions. A lone gnome on the road might be seeking materials, investigating a mystery or looking for someone who appreciates their work. Curiosity can lead to courage as well as carelessness. They usually want to create safely, learn and share their results with people they trust.

Cleverness improves one Intelligence result outside a direct attack once per scene, while Rune Resistance increases magic defense. A gnome therefore offers more than a small warrior: problem-solving and resistance to magic are their strengths. The party may need an explanation of a strange mechanism, help with research or assistance finding a missing apprentice. A gnome settlement may be friendly, but it need not grant access to sensitive knowledge to everyone who can pay.

strings.1× za scénu získá +2 k jednomu výsledku: Once per scene, gains +2 to one Intelligence result outside a direct attack. Gains +2 MDEF against magical attacks.

best/kentaur.name: Centaur
profile: Centaurs combine a human upper body with the build of a horse and seek open country in Elaria. They live on grassy plains, in broad valleys and at forest edges where they have room to move. Their traditions are tied to travel, the landscape and their family's collective memory. Changes to paths, pastures and water sources therefore affect their lives more directly than distant borders on someone else's map.

They are intelligent inhabitants of the world with their own opinions and culture. They may form family groups led by elders or an experienced leader, although a wandering centaur can also travel alone. They seek safe territory, freedom of movement and agreements that are honored. Their behavior toward strangers reflects past experiences. Blocking a traditional route or threatening a water source can cause a conflict that surprises neighboring settlements but makes perfect sense to a centaur.

Charge strengthens their first attack after an unobstructed running start. Open space therefore supports their fighting style, while cramped passages and obstacles restrict their movement. The party can gain a guide, negotiate passage or help resolve a dispute over the landscape. A centaur may fight fiercely to defend their group, but remains capable of agreement and changing their position. Respecting their space and customs is usually a better beginning than treating them as a riding animal.

strings.V prvním kole po volném rozběhu získá +2: During the first round, after an unobstructed running start, gains +2 to the final Attack result.

best/minotaur.name: Minotaur
profile: A minotaur is a powerful humanoid with a bull's head and horns. In Elaria, it can be encountered in deep ruins, rocky strongholds and complex underground structures. Legends attribute ancient curses to some families and origins in forgotten cultures to others. Its association with labyrinths may come from its actual home or from stories told by people who could not find their way out of its territory.

It may live alone, protect a family group or guard an important location. Strength and appearance do not make it a mindless creature. It can make decisions, recognize familiar people and uphold its own commitments. Its goal may be the safety of its home, fulfilling an oath or protecting something others do not understand. Some minotaurs are violent attackers, while others use their intimidating presence to prevent combat altogether.

After a powerful hit, Horned Charge can weaken the target's next attack. Bull's Endurance reduces the first physical and first magical damage each round, with each counted separately. A direct confrontation therefore requires a plan and a good understanding of the rules. The party can seek another entrance, discover the conditions of the guardian's oath or present proof of their right to pass. It has no automatically assigned weakness to a particular substance; its actual vulnerability may depend on the specific story and surroundings.

strings.1× za souboj může místo sekery zaútočit: Once per combat, may attack with horns +4 instead of an axe. If it deals at least 3 damage, the target gets −2 Attack next round. Reduces the first physical and first magical damage taken each round by 4, counted separately (minimum 0).

best/obr.name: Giant
profile: Giants inhabit mountainous regions, vast wastelands and places with enough space and food for their size. Their buildings look rough and excessively large to human visitors, yet may follow their own order and craft traditions. Elaria has legends of ancient giant families whose homes others now mistake for natural rock formations. A solitary giant may descend from such a family or have been exiled from their own group.

They live alone, with family or in a small community. Leadership may depend on age, strength or respected experience. A giant understands their needs and relationships; slower actions or different customs are not evidence of an inability to think. They seek food, peace and safe territory. What they consider ordinary provisions or a clear path may, however, mean an entire herd or a roof over someone's head to a human.

Wide Swing attacks two targets once per combat with separate, weakened attacks. Massive Body reduces every instance of physical damage, while magical damage is not reduced in this way. The party can use the terrain, keep out of reach or try to clarify a dispute before the giant's size advantage comes into play. A giant may need help with a missing relative or a threat to their cave. Agreement is possible if both sides understand what the other actually wants.

strings.1× za souboj zaútočí na 2 cíle; proti ka: Once per combat, attacks 2 targets, rolling separately against each with −2 to the final Attack result. Reduces each instance of physical damage by 2 (minimum 0); magical damage is not reduced.

best/troll.name: Troll
profile: A troll seeks damp forests, swamps, rocky fissures and abandoned underground spaces. In Elaria, stories about its origins involve wild magic and ancient transformations of the landscape. It may change its territory according to available food, but returns to a safe den. Remains of prey, broken branches and enormous tracks warn that something roams nearby that ordinary animals prefer to avoid.

It often lives alone, although trolls sometimes gather or answer to a stronger leader. It can remember successful hunting grounds, recognize recurring threats and try simple ways to obtain food. Hunger, defending a shelter or payment for service may motivate it. Not every troll is willing to talk, and not every offer will stop it, but a story can give an individual a comprehensible reason for blocking the road.

Regeneration restores two Health at the start of its turn if it has taken no magical damage since the end of its previous turn. Tough Hide also reduces the first physical damage each round. It is therefore important to maintain pressure and use the actual weakness in the rules: magical damage interrupts its recovery, and it need not be fire. The party can go around the troll, draw it away from the place it protects or discover who supplies it. A reputation for invincibility often develops because previous opponents did not understand its regeneration.

strings.Na začátku svého tahu obnoví 2 Ž, pokud: At the start of its turn, restores 2 HP if it has taken no magical damage since the end of its previous turn. Tough Hide reduces the first physical damage it takes each round by 2 (minimum 0).

best/kostlivec.name: Skeleton
profile: A skeleton is the remains of a dead body set in motion by necromancy, a curse or an ancient ward protecting a place. It can be encountered in tombs, on abandoned battlefields and in buildings where an order outlasted the guards who died. Its equipment may point to a former garrison and help establish the undead creature's origins. The bones alone, however, do not reveal whether an order, an object or someone still controlling it is the key.

It usually has no ordinary human needs and does not act from hunger or a desire for payment. It may repeat a simple task, guard a boundary or follow a necromancer's will. A lone skeleton is often a guardian; several undead may form a line, patrol or group ready to respond to a single command. Its apparent patience comes from not needing to sleep or make decisions like a living person. Aggression often begins when a specific condition is met, such as entering a guarded room.

Bones reduces physical damage from a dagger or arrow by one. This does not mean complete invulnerability or protection against all physical weapons. The party can seek safe passage, the origin of the order or the reason skeletons have awakened now. An emblem on a shield or a repeated movement may provide a clue. Lifting a curse or changing control requires the adventure's specific conditions; simply talking to a creature mechanically following an order may not be enough.

strings.Snižuje každé fyzické zranění z dýky neb: Reduces each instance of physical damage from a dagger or arrow by 1 (minimum 0).

best/kostlivec-lucistnik.name: Skeleton Archer
profile: A skeleton archer is an animated bowman who continues defending an assigned place even after death. It may stand on the walls of a ruined fortress, in a tomb gallery or behind an arrow slit long forgotten by the living garrison. Its bow, insignia or remaining equipment may reveal whom the original soldier served. Magic may preserve an old order or place it under a new master's control.

It does not act according to a living archer's ordinary needs. It may wait motionless until someone enters a defined area, then respond in the same way each time. Within a group, its fire can be combined with skeletons guarding the approach. A necromancer, curse or magical ward may control it. The degree of its own will depends on its specific origin; the stat profile alone does not mean it carries the original person's memories.

Like an ordinary skeleton, it reduces damage from a dagger or arrow by one. At range, it benefits from its position and an unobstructed view, so cover and another route can significantly change an encounter. It does not automatically have the same special abilities as a living archer. The party can investigate what triggers its fire, whose insignia it wears and whether a legitimate way to enter exists. Discovering the guard's origins can explain why it defends something that now seems entirely worthless.

strings.Snižuje každé fyzické zranění z dýky neb: Reduces each instance of physical damage from a dagger or arrow by 1 (minimum 0).

best/zombie.name: Zombie
profile: A zombie is a dead body kept moving by dark magic or a curse. It may rise in a graveyard, underground, or at the site of an ancient disaster; its creation often involves someone or something that disturbed the peace of the dead. Decaying equipment, a personal possession, or a familiar face can connect the threat to a settlement's past. A zombie represents both a danger and a person whose story did not end with dignity.

Most zombies have little will of their own. They follow orders, repeat simple actions, or react to the presence of the living according to the nature of their animation. One may wander alone, while a group controlled by a necromancer pursues a shared goal. Their lack of fear and fatigue makes them persistent, but they cannot normally reassess a situation or negotiate as a living person would. A zombie bound to an unusually powerful memory or curse may be an exception.

Relentless means that the first time the zombie would drop to zero HP, it remains at one HP; the second time, it falls normally. It can therefore appear defeated before it actually stops being a threat. Its rules do not automatically give it an infectious bite or require a weakness to blows to the head. The party can separate a group, secure an escape route, or seek the source of its animation. Investigating the past and removing the cause may matter more than destroying more bodies that keep returning.

strings.Poprvé, kdy by klesla na 0 Ž, zůstane na: The first time it would drop to 0 HP, it remains at 1 HP; the second time, it falls normally.

best/ghul.name: Ghoul
profile: A ghoul is an undead creature associated with death, decay, and disturbed graves. In Elaria, it inhabits tombs, devastated settlements, and underground places where dark magic lingers. Various curses or prolonged exposure to necromancy may explain its creation. Unsettling tracks lead to opened graves, remains of bodies, and places where people disappear after setting out to find a missing relative.

Unlike an undead creature carrying out a single command, a ghoul may act as a hunter driven by its own predatory hunger. It is alert and can wait for the right moment, but its story determines how much reason and memory it retains. It may act alone, form a group with other ghouls, or serve a necromancer who exploits its hunger. A living person usually represents prey or an obstacle. An encounter is therefore dangerous even without an openly hostile former master.

Once per battle, Paralyzing Chill temporarily reduces a target's attack and defense after a damaging hit. A weakened ally may quickly need cover and help from the others. The ability does not automatically cause complete paralysis or turn its victim into another ghoul. The party can secure the area, uncover the source of the curse, or rescue someone still surviving underground. If a particular ghoul retains fragments of its identity, a personal possession may provide a story clue; its effect must arise from that adventure.

strings.1× za souboj, pokud způsobí zranění, má: Once per battle, if it deals damage, the target suffers −1 to ATTACK and DEFENSE until the end of the next round.

best/duch.name: Ghost
profile: A ghost is the lingering, incorporeal presence of a person or another being whose story remained unfinished after death. A place, an object, an unfulfilled promise, or a violent deed may bind it. In Elaria, ghosts appear in houses, on old roads, and among ruins where the living overlooked an event that remained crucial to the dead. A chill, a recurring sound, or an appearing figure may point to the final moments of its life.

Its level of awareness varies. One ghost can speak and learn new facts, while another simply repeats an event or responds to a particular stimulus. It is usually connected to its own past, but may be influenced by a curse or someone else's magic. It need not be aggressive: it may seek a witness, protect a place, or try to warn others of danger. Visitors' fear and misunderstanding of its actions can turn a message into a conflict.

Incorporeal reduces each instance of physical damage by two, while magical damage is not reduced. A ghost is therefore not completely invulnerable, but ordinary weapons lose effectiveness against it. The party can try to discover its name, the cause of its death, and the meaning of its recurring manifestation. Fulfilling a promise or uncovering the truth may bring peace if this fits the particular story. A reasoning ghost can provide information the living lack, but should not automatically know everything that has happened since its death.

Reduces each instance of physical damage by 2 (minimum 0); magical damage is not reduced.

best/prizrak.name: Wraith
profile: A wraith arises where death, a curse, or dark magic accumulated over time has created an especially dangerous presence. In Elaria, it lingers in places associated with fear and violence: abandoned fortresses, desecrated shrines, and underground chambers people no longer visit. Its appearance may resemble the person it once was, or merely a shadow retaining a few recognizable features.

It often acts with greater purpose and menace than a ghost repeating a memory. It may guard a secret, pursue revenge, or serve whoever summoned it. Sometimes it acts independently; sometimes it forms part of a wider curse. Its intelligence and capacity for conversation depend on its origin: powerful anger can suppress everything except a single purpose. It need not attack everyone indiscriminately if a particular act or identity triggers its threat.

Chilling Touch allows it to make a magical attack, while Partial Incorporeality reduces physical damage by one. This protection does not reduce magical damage. The party must therefore account for an attack against which physical defense is not the primary protection. Investigating the site may reveal what binds the wraith and whom it is actually seeking. Breaking its bond, righting a wrong, or safely bypassing the place may offer a solution, but the story must determine the conditions rather than a general superstition about all undead.

strings.Může místo fyzického útoku použít magick: May use a magical attack with a spell bonus of +3 instead of a physical attack. Reduces each instance of physical damage by 1 (minimum 0); magical damage is not reduced.

best/mumie.name: Mummy
profile: A mummy is a preserved body set in motion after death by a curse, necromancy, or an ancient protective spell. Its home is usually a tomb, a temple's underground chambers, or a burial structure from a forgotten culture. Its wrappings, jewelry, and inscriptions can reveal its origin and the dead person's former status. Opening the tomb may activate defenses created for a world with very different rules from present-day Elaria.

It may be a guardian, an executor of orders, or a being that retains some memories. One protects burial goods; another seeks an object taken from its tomb. A solitary mummy may represent a buried ruler, while several mummies may be attendants or guards. Their control may depend on an ancient ritual or a present-day necromancer. Aggression often follows an intrusion into a protected place rather than a need for food or ordinary prey.

Once per battle, Curse temporarily worsens all of the target's final rolls after a damaging hit. Ancient Protection increases magical defense, so magic alone may not be an easy solution. This effect does not automatically constitute a permanent disease, and the profile specifies no special weakness to fire. The party can translate inscriptions, return a stolen object, or seek a way to enter legitimately. Understanding the burial rules can turn seemingly senseless violence into a solvable dispute about what was promised to the dead.

strings.1× za souboj po úspěšném zranění má cíl: Once per battle, after a damaging hit, the target suffers −1 to all final rolls until the end of the next round. Against magical attacks, the mummy has +2 MDEF.

best/upir.name: Vampire
profile: A vampire is an intelligent undead being that may retain the memories, skills, and ambitions of its former life. In Elaria, its creation involves a curse, a dark ritual, or another vampire, depending on the particular character's story. It seeks a secure refuge protected from direct sunlight: underground chambers, a remote estate, or a carefully managed house. It need not appear obviously monstrous; polished manners and long experience can help it conceal its true nature.

It may live alone, maintain a network of servants, or belong to a group with its own leadership and rules. It seeks blood or life force, safety, and a way to preserve its influence. It understands people and may exploit them, but its personality, relationships, and boundaries vary. Tales about garlic, holy water, invitations into houses, or special methods of destruction differ from region to region. They can guide an investigation, but their actual effectiveness must be established for the particular vampire in that adventure.

Under these rules, its actual weakness is direct sunlight. In sunlight, the reduction of the first instance of physical and magical damage does not apply, physical and magical defense both drop by four, and it cannot use Life Drain. In shade, a damaging fang attack can restore three HP once per battle. The party can plan the time and place of a confrontation, search for victims, or uncover its network. Negotiation is possible with a being that understands its own interests, but its long-term plan may extend beyond a short-lived promise.

strings.1× za souboj, pokud tesáky způsobí alesp: Once per battle, if its fangs deal at least 2 damage, it restores 3 HP. Reduces the first instance of physical damage and the first instance of magical damage each round by 2 (minimum 0). In direct sunlight, this reduction does not apply, it suffers −4 PDEF and MDEF, and it cannot use Life Drain.
strings.Sání života; Nadpřirozená odolnost a slu: Life Drain; Supernatural Resilience and Sunlight Weakness

best/nekromant.name: Necromancer
profile: A necromancer is a living magic user who studies death, remains, and the forces that can keep undead bodies moving. This knowledge may come from forbidden books, a secret teacher, or personal research. In Elaria, a necromancer seeks a secluded base near tombs, battlefields, and other places associated with the dead, but may also work in a city under another guise. Signs of this activity include disturbed graves, unusual orders, and the repeated disappearance of particular kinds of objects.

Necromancers are intelligent and capable of planning. One may work alone, lead apprentices, or serve a more powerful patron; undead creatures can be guards as well as a means of labor. Their motives may include power, knowledge, fear of death, or an attempt to bring back someone they lost. Such a motive explains their actions without justifying the consequences. The particular adventure determines the extent of their control over undead and rituals; this combat profile does not grant it automatically.

Dark Blast provides a magical attack, while Dark Shield increases defense against the first magical attack of each round. A necromancer can therefore be dangerous even without servants. The party can uncover the base, interrupt preparations, or discover who supplies the resources. Conversation may reveal a condition the necromancer refuses to abandon and a weakness in the plan. If personal loss drives the work, offering another solution may change the situation; if the aim is to dominate the region, information may merely help buy time.

strings.1; spíš obejít/slabina: 1; bypassing or exploiting a weakness preferred
strings.Může používat magický útok s bonusem kou: May use a magical attack with a spell bonus of +3. Has +3 MDEF against the first magical attack each round.

best/obri-had.name: Giant Snake
profile: A giant snake seeks places with plenty of cover and large prey: wetlands, dense vegetation, warm rock cavities, and overgrown ruins. In Elaria, its unusual size may result from local conditions, magic, or ancient breeding, depending on the particular creature's origin. A wide trail through soft ground, shed skin, and missing animals warn that the familiar image of a small snake does not apply.

It usually lives alone. It senses movement and its surroundings, conserves its strength, and waits for prey to come close. No social leader directs it unless someone influences it through a specific form of magic. Its main motivations are food, safety, and defending its shelter. Noise, disturbing its lair, or blocking its retreat may provoke an attack even when it was not originally hunting.

Potent Venom takes effect only if the bite actually deals damage; the victim loses two more HP at the end of the next round, and the effect does not stack. Plans for help and retreat must account for this delayed damage. The profile does not automatically add grappling or constriction. The party can find another route, establish why the snake is there, or secure a path around its hunting ground. A snake that suddenly appears near a settlement may point to a disturbed marsh or someone who brought it there as a dangerous guard.

strings.Pokud uštknutí způsobí alespoň 1 zranění: If its bite deals at least 1 damage, the target loses 2 HP at the end of the next round; the effect does not stack.

best/obri-pavouk.name: Giant Spider
profile: A giant spider inhabits caves, overgrown forests, underground spaces, and abandoned buildings where it can anchor its web. In Elaria, it may belong to a wild population or come from a place long affected by magic. Remnants of webbing, wrapped prey, and faintly trembling strands warn of its presence. A web is more than an obstacle: it can help the spider detect movement in areas it cannot see directly.

It acts primarily as a hunter. It often lives alone, although a larger infestation may contain several individuals and their young. It has no interest in human wealth or ordinary revenge; prey, safety, and defending its shelter explain most of its behavior. It can wait patiently and strike only when its target is at a disadvantage. If it serves another being, the particular story must explain how it is controlled.

After a damaging bite from its mandibles, Venom causes an additional loss of HP at the end of the next round. Once per battle, Web temporarily reduces the target's defense by two; it does not automatically immobilize the target completely. The combination makes an isolated character vulnerable. The party can examine the webs' anchor points, choose another route, or free a victim who is still alive. A sudden spread of spiders may indicate an abandoned space, a change in available food, or the opening of underground chambers that should have remained sealed.

strings.Po zranění kusadly cíl ztratí 1 Ž na kon: After taking damage from its mandibles, the target loses 1 HP at the end of the next round. Once per battle, its web may impose −2 DEFENSE on the target until the end of the target's next turn.

best/harpyje.name: Harpy
profile: A harpy is a winged creature with humanoid features that inhabits high cliffs, mountain gorges, and ruins above difficult terrain. In Elaria, old tales of transformations and wild magic offer different explanations for its origins. Its nesting place may contain remains of prey and objects carried from nearby roads. Strange singing heard among the rocks may be the party's first warning that it has entered harpy territory.

A harpy may act alone or in a small group. It can choose an advantageous position and exploit whatever draws visitors' attention. Some groups have dominant individuals; others cooperate loosely according to the availability of prey and safety. Food, protecting a nest, or acquiring interesting objects may motivate it. Intelligence and the possibility of negotiation vary with the particular harpy, which may see strangers as threats, opportunities, or sources of information.

Once per battle, Luring Song functions as a magical attack that deals no damage. If it overcomes magical defense, it weakens the target's next attack by two. This does not automatically mean complete control or a command to jump from a cliff. Height and broken terrain nevertheless make the encounter dangerous in their own right. The party can seek another approach, discover why the road is being attacked, or negotiate the return of an object. The song may also reveal the location of a nest that can be avoided.

strings.1× za souboj provede magický útok s bonu: Once per battle, makes a magical attack with a +2 bonus; if it overcomes the target's MDEF, the target suffers −2 to ATTACK in the next round. Deals no damage.

best/gryfon.name: Griffin
profile: A griffin combines the powerful body of a beast with the wings and head of a bird of prey. In Elaria, it nests on cliffs, in mountain regions, and above open country from which it can watch for prey. It needs space to take flight and a safe place for its young. Large feathers, claw marks, and remains of prey in places ordinary ground predators cannot easily reach reveal its presence.

It behaves as an alert hunter and a protector of its nesting place. It may live alone, in a pair, or with young still unable to feed themselves. A human commander does not naturally direct it. If it was raised in cooperation with people, that relationship and trust need a real foundation in the story. A wild griffin seeks food and safety; it may regard strangers near its nest as a direct threat.

Once per battle, Dive Attack strengthens a strike but then temporarily reduces the griffin's physical defense. Airspace, cover, and the positions of the other party members significantly affect the encounter. An interesting expedition might involve finding a stolen egg, rescuing an injured griffin, or passing safely beneath its nest. Offering food alone does not guarantee obedience. A griffin deserves treatment appropriate to a powerful wild creature whose decisions cannot be bought with a single gesture.

strings.1× za souboj získá +2 k výslednému ÚTOKU: Once per battle, gains +2 to its final ATTACK; afterward, it suffers −1 PDEF until its next turn.

best/bazilisek.name: Basilisk
profile: A basilisk is a dangerous scaled creature whose presence turns an ordinary exploration of ruins into an exceptionally cautious expedition. In Elaria, it inhabits rock cavities, dry ravines, and underground spaces. Tales link its origins to ancient magical transformations. An unusually empty territory, remains of prey, and figures resembling petrified witnesses may suggest it is nearby, but the particular site's history still needs investigation.

It generally lives alone and reacts as a hunter or a defender of its territory. It does not seek treasure for its monetary value or follow human orders without a special reason. It may remember safe hunting grounds and return to places where prey cannot escape. Keeping a basilisk as a guardian is dangerous for its keeper and may explain why the creature has appeared near an important building.

Once per battle, Petrifying Gaze attempts to overcome magical defense; an affected target cannot attack in the next round but defends normally, and the effect deals no damage. The basic profile does not make this permanent petrification. Magic Scales also increase the basilisk's magical defense. The party can seek a safe route or discover who brought the creature there. Legends about mirrors and similar tricks may inspire an attempt, but their effectiveness requires specific conditions established by the adventure.

strings.1× za souboj provede magický útok s bonu: Once per battle, makes a magical attack with a +3 bonus; if it overcomes the target's MDEF, the target cannot attack in the next round but defends normally. Deals no damage. Against magical attacks, the basilisk has +2 MDEF.

best/kamenny-golem.name: Stone Golem
profile: A stone golem is an artificial guardian whose body is held together by magic and a runic core. It may come from a mage's workshop, a temple, or an ancient culture that needed protection lasting beyond a human lifetime. In Elaria, it guards gates, vaults, corridors, and forgotten halls. Its material, inscriptions, and workmanship may reveal its creator and original purpose, even when the surrounding building has changed beyond recognition.

It usually follows defined instructions. It needs no food, reward, or ordinary rest, and may not understand changes outside the scope of its orders. It can remain motionless until someone meets an activation condition. One golem protects a particular entrance; several may form an entire defensive system. Depending on its creation, it is directed by a present master, its original command, or a means of control.

Stone Body reduces each instance of physical damage by two. If a single magical attack deals at least four damage, this reduction does not apply until the start of the golem's next round; this is the precise combat vulnerability of its Runic Core. The party can investigate the conditions for passage, seek a mark of authorization, or discover a flaw in an old order. A control stone or password may exist, but the story determines its form. A golem need not be evil: it may faithfully protect something whose true significance the living have forgotten.

Reduces each instance of physical damage by 2 (minimum 0). If a single magical attack deals at least 4 damage, this reduction does not apply until the start of the golem's next round.

best/elemental.name: Elemental
profile: An elemental is a being shaped by the power of a single element, such as fire, water, earth, or air. In Elaria, it may arise where magic is exceptionally concentrated or be summoned through a ritual. Its body behaves according to the nature of its element and need not resemble any familiar animal. Changes in temperature, currents, moisture, or the movement of material around it may defy ordinary conditions.

It may act on a simple need of its own, defend its place, or follow its summoner's command. Its perception is not necessarily human: what a person sees as destruction, an elemental may experience as natural expansion or renewal. Encounters usually involve a single being, but a severely disturbed place may attract several similar creatures. The possibility of conversation, the duration of a summoning, and its obligation to a master depend on its particular origin.

Elemental Blast allows a magical attack. Elemental Essence normally increases magical defense by two; against magic clearly representing its element's natural opposite, its magical defense is instead reduced by two. Identifying the creature's nature before a confrontation is therefore important. The party can seek the source of a disturbance, restore the site's balance, or uncover the conditions of the summoning. The mere presence of ordinary water or soil does not automatically have the same effect as an appropriate magical attack.

strings.Může používat magický útok s bonusem kou: May use a magical attack with a spell bonus of +3. Has +2 MDEF against magical attacks. Against magic clearly representing its element's natural opposite, it instead suffers −2 MDEF.

best/chimera.name: Chimera
profile: A chimera is a monster whose body combines features of several different creatures. In Elaria, its creation is attributed to wild magic, ancient experiments, and regions where the natural order has long been changing. It settles among remote rocks, in caves, and in ruins with plenty of space. Mismatched tracks and unusual remains of prey may confuse the party, as though several different predators inhabited the site.

Individual chimeras may differ in appearance, but this combat profile focuses on fierce physical attacks. It is usually a solitary hunter and defender of its territory. When seeking food, it uses strength, movement, and surprise; it need not be capable of complex human interactions. Anyone breeding or controlling it needs a specific means and purpose. Hunger, injury, or the loss of a lair may explain attacks beyond its original territory.

Once per battle, Double Strike allows two physical attacks in one turn, each with a reduced final attack result. The party must account for this sudden increase in pressure on its defenses. The profile does not automatically add dragon breath or other abilities associated with every possible head; those would belong to a special variant. Investigating the chimera's origins may lead to an abandoned laboratory or a disturbed site. A safe detour or removing the cause of its migration may save a nearby settlement without another direct confrontation.

strings.1× za souboj provede 2 fyzické útoky v j: Once per battle, makes 2 physical attacks in one turn, but each suffers −2 to its final ATTACK.

best/hydra.name: Hydra
profile: A hydra is a massive, many-headed monster that seeks wetlands, flooded caves, and remote valleys with abundant food. In Elaria, its origins are associated with ancient watery depths and places marked by powerful magic. Torn-up banks, several attack marks on a single prey animal, and an unusually deserted watering place may reveal its hunting grounds. Its presence can close an entire important route.

It usually lives alone, asserting itself through its size and several heads watching different directions. This does not imply several independent personalities capable of human conversation. It behaves as a dangerous hunter and defender of its territory, requiring large amounts of food. A particular story may connect it to a keeper, a curse, or the protection of an ancient site; any means of directing it must be explained, since an ordinary monster has no reason to obey strangers' orders.

Many Heads allows it to attack two different targets each round, both with a weakened attack. Tenacious Necks reduces the first two instances of damage each round by three, so the hydra's defenses do not rely solely on its high HP.
